[[File:Dirk van Dalen.jpg|thumb|215px|Dirk van Dalen]]
'''Dirk van Dalen''' (born 20 December 1932, [[Amsterdam]]) is a [[Dutch people|Dutch]] [[mathematician]] and [[historian]] of science.

== Life ==

Van Dalen studied mathematics and physics and astronomy at the [[University of Amsterdam]]. Inspired by the work of [[LEJ Brouwer|Brouwer]] and [[Arend Heyting|Heyting]], he received his Ph.D. in 1963 from the University of Amsterdam for the thesis ''Extension problems in intuitionistic plane Projective geometry''.{{sfn|Van Dalen|1963}} From 1964 to 1966 Van Dalen taught [[mathematical logic|logic]] and mathematics at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], and later [[University of Oxford|Oxford]]. From 1967 he was professor at the [[University of Utrecht]]. In 2003 Dirk van Dalen was awarded the Academy Medal 2003 of the [[Royal Dutch Academy of Sciences]] for bringing the works of Brouwer to international attention.{{sfn|KNAW|2003}}
